records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without optional access or fallback, throwing when the attendee list is empty
records.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email subject builds `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without checking that `this.calEvent.attendees` has at least one element. If `attendees` is empty, this will throw at runtime when generating the email payload. The diff does not guarantee `attendees` is non-empty for all calls to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

records.issue_text: Error message template string in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is always non-empty, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and showing raw `undefined: ...` codes
records.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. A template literal always produces a non-empty string even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined`, resulting in e.g. `"undefined: ..."`. Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` will never hit the fallback, making it dead code and potentially showing a raw/incorrect error

records.issue_text: Email failures are swallowed with `console.log` without logging the error object, making delivery failures undiagnosable
records.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` is wrapped in a `try/catch`, but the `catch (err)` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err` or rethrowing. This suppresses actionable error details and makes email delivery failures difficult to diagnose.
